key_insights: CMBI Total Market index at 595.55, down 0.83% week over week. BGCI Index at $2,100, down 1.74% WoW.
CMBI Bitcoin at $80,764, down 0.71% WoW, with a 56.0% share of total crypto market cap. CMBI Ethereum at $2,331, down 2.15% WoW, with a 9.81% share.
Binance lost over $6 billion in what the headline calls the biggest crypto hack in history.

NYSE parent ICE is moving to bring Hyperliquid perpetual futures to the US and will take a strategic stake in TradeXYZ. Kraken parent Payward is to be the first CFTC-regulated HIP-3 deployer on Hyperliquid.
Ripple received final OCC approval to establish a national trust bank. Moody's assigned investment-grade ratings to Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin.
Polymarket resumed trading after a $2.65 million exploit, saying a third-party provider was compromised.
Crypto.com and OG.com launched US crypto perpetual futures.
HSBC rolled out its first HKD stablecoin, RedCoin, to retail users.
Strategy reported $19.5 billion in Q3 net income, and preferred shareholders approved daily dividends.

Tokenization: DTCC's tokenization service went live on Canton Network and private chain Besu. J.P. Morgan Asset Management expanded access to its tokenized money market funds on Solana. Aviva Investors is tokenising its largest fund. BlackRock, SBI Holdings and Startale signed an MOU to bridge tokenized MMFs and a yen stablecoin (JPYSC).
DBS reports nearly 90% of large businesses are embracing tokenized cash to speed up payments.

Regulation: South Korea is weighing a fourth delay of its crypto gains tax, with a 2029 start under consideration. South Korea plans to amend its forex law to regulate stablecoins as payment instruments. Canada opened a consultation on draft stablecoin rules and maintains its ban on yields.
